edges.description: Complete adult loss of core 1 O-glycans reproduces the multisystem consequences, including thrombocytopenia and kidney dysfunction.
edges.limitations: The knockout removes Cosmc entirely, whereas patients have reduced but present Cosmc and residual T-synthase; the mice die within days with pancreatitis and gastric ulcers, which are not features of the patients.

nodes.description: In the child with the de novo p.Thr89Ile variant, erythrocytes display exposed T antigen, an unmasked O-glycan structure. This differs from the Tn-antigen finding in the p.Ala20Asp family, whose cells were studied as lymphoblasts and mononuclear cells, so the erythrocyte observation comes from one patient. The authors propose that this exposed glycan triggers complement through the lectin pathway, as suggested for Streptococcus pneumoniae-associated HUS.

nodes.description: During acute kidney injury episodes the alternative pathway shows consumption (low C3, raised sC5b-9). The first aHUS8 report proposes that exposed erythrocyte glycans activate the lectin pathway, as suggested for pneumococcal HUS; the lectin pathway was not measured, so it is recorded as a hypothesis and the node is bound to the alternative pathway that was measured. Anti-galactose-deficient-IgA1 immune complexes and glycan-defective endothelium are other untested possible triggers.

nodes.description: De novo mosaic nonsense variant (c.202C>T) in a girl, detected at a 27% allelic fraction in buccal cells, which the paper converts to about 54% of cells carrying it; the truncated Cosmc is nonfunctional. It arose very early after fertilization, so it is not a germline variant. She presented with nonimmune hydrops fetalis of unknown cause, has persistent proteinuria with normal renal function and normal C3 and C4, and also carries a paternally inherited likely pathogenic IRF2BPL variant, so her phenotype is not attributed to the disorder here.
